feedback.problem:
Use the definition of Laplace transforms to calculate $F(s)=L{f(t)},$ where $f(t)$ is given by 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}3,\, & t\le 5 \\ {e}^{3t}\, & t>5.\end{aligned}
$$

$\,F(s)=L{f(t)}=$ {{field-1}},
valid for {{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We apply the definition of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =F(s)={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

So, for the piecewise function 

$$
f(t)={\begin{aligned}3,\, & t\le 5 \\ {e}^{3t}\, & t>5\end{aligned}
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }f(t){e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}3\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{5}^{\infty }{e}^{3t}\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}3\cdot {e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{5}^{\infty }{e}^{3t-st}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}3{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{5}^{\infty }{e}^{(3-s)t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the improper integral diverges if $s\le 3.$

For $s>3,$ we calculate our Laplace transform as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & ={\int }_{0}^{5}3{e}^{-st}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{5}^{\infty }{e}^{(3-s)t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{3}{s}{[{e}^{-st}]}_{0}^{5}+{\int }_{5}^{\infty }{e}^{(3-s)t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{3}{s}-\frac{3{e}^{-5s}}{s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{5}^{a}{e}^{(3-s)t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{3}{s}-\frac{3{e}^{-5s}}{s}+{lim}_{a\to \infty }{(\frac{{e}^{(3-s)t}}{3-s})|}_{5}^{a} \\  & =\frac{3}{s}-\frac{3{e}^{-5s}}{s}+\frac{1}{3-s}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }({e}^{(3-s)a}-{e}^{5(3-s)}) \\  & =\frac{3}{s}-\frac{3{e}^{-5s}}{s}+\frac{1}{3-s}\cdot (0-{e}^{5(3-s)}) \\  & =\frac{3}{s}-\frac{3{e}^{-5s}}{s}+\frac{{e}^{5(3-s)}}{s-3}\end{aligned}
$$

valid for $s>3.$
